sentences.text:
The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 23-2-2021 at about 8.30 a.m. when the petitioner was riding his splender pro motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-53-EJ- 9918 on New BEL road, near H.P. Petrol bunk, Bengaluru from north to south direction i.e., from Kuvempu circle side towards Ramaiah junction, at that time, driver of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371 came from his behind at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle to its right side, as a result petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and motor cycle was also damaged badly.
It is further stated that petitioner took treatment at hospital as inpatient and spent money for treatment.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, working as Interior wood work supervisor at Gopalan Enterprises and getting salary of Rs.25000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, he is permanently disabled and lost his income.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte and respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. Respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that the policy particular mentioned in petition OG- 18-1701-1831-00000153 is issued to vehicle No.DL-1-RY-4747 from 8-5-2017 to 7-5-2018 only and this does not cover date of accident that is 23-2-2021 and no policy is issued to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
The policy coverage details mentioned in the petition are false and fabricated and not issued by this respondent.
The owner of the vehicle has not submitted the claim form and other documents like RC,DL, permit etc., for verification.
On the date of accident, offending vehicle was not holding effective DL which is in contravention of the conditions and MV Act.

The offending vehicle was having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply in the public place, in this regard jurisdictional police have fled charge sheet u/s 66 and 192 of MV Act and there is a violation of provisions of MV Act.
The petitioner has suppressed the true fact and colluded with the first respondent and jurisdictional police and filed false case against the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371.

The petitioner was not wearing safety head gear at the Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
2 time of alleged accident.

5. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the autrickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371 on 23-2-2021 at about 8.30 a.m. at New BEL road, near HP, petrol bunk, Bengaluru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and in his support P.W.2 to 4 are examined.
Exs. P1
to P95
documents are marked.

The respondent No.2 got examined one Jayanth Inamadar-Manager legal in respondent No.2 company as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1 to Ex-R3.
7.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 95 documents as Ex- P1 to 95 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch,
notice under col.133, reply to notice, IMV report, charge sheet, ordersheet in CC No.1647/21, wound certificate, discharge summary, record showing treatment at Multispeciality hospital, medical prescriptions, medical bills, aadhaar card, pan card, DL, form No.6, x-rays, advance medical bills.
10.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of the vehicle, cause and occurrence of the accident.

The counsel for the respondent No.2 has taken the contention that the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD- 5371 is not at all involved in the accident and same is implicated in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to the second respondent.
And all the police records are manipulated.

The evidence on records shows that after lodging of the complaint by petitioner, Sadashivanagar traffic police have registered FIR as per Ex-P1 against the Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
3 driver of the offending vehicle autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371.

sentences.text:
Thereafter after conducting thorough and detailed investigation filed the charge sheet as per Ex-P9 by holding that on 23-2- 2021 at about 8.30 a.m. driver of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371 drove his auto in BEL road from Isro junction towards MSR junction in high speed, rash and negligent manner and near HP petrol bunk without giving any indicator and signal suddenly drove his vehicle towards left side of the road and hit to the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-EJ-9918 who was moving on the left side of the auto and due to impact, the petitioner fell on the ground along with motor cycle and sustained grievous injuries. Accordingly it was held that the accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371.
11.

Though counsel for the respondent No.2 argued that there was a delay of one day, but MLC produced Ex-P86 clearly shows that petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 23-2- 2021 soon after the accident at 1 p.m. and the history of the injuries is clearly mentioned as history of RTA near BEL road on 23-2-2021 at 8.30 a.m. and he was rider of the two wheeler and was hit by the autorickhaw.
Ex-P86 and 87 MLC clearly shows that there was an accident between two wheeler of the petitioner and autorickshaw and involvement of the vehicle.

12. Apart from this, petitioner has produced Ex-P3 spot mahazar, Ex-P4 sketch, it clearly shows that spot of accident is the junction and the accident had been taken place in the middle of the road where there was a turn towards the left side.

Further Ex-P4 clearly shows that the accident had been taken place as the driver of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03- AD-5371 has suddenly taken the turn towards left without giving any indication to the vehicles moving behind and beside him.

Though respondent has disputed the occurrence and involvement of the vehicle, but has not examined the driver of the auto who is material eye witness to disprove the evidence of PW-1 or to prove his contention.
Though respondent No.2 has examined the Legal Manager of the insurance company as RW-1, but RW-1 is not an eye witness.
Apart from this, there is no material to prove that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Ex. P7 and 8 IMV reports indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently, I hold Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
4 that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371.
15.

ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16.
ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 38 years.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card, pan card, DL, form No.6 as per Ex.P.68 to 71, it reveals the date of birth of the petitioner was 4-5-1982.
So, as on the date of accident 23-2-2021 the petitioner was aged 38 years 09 months, 19 days.

The petitioner has stated that he was working as Interior woodwork supervisor at Gopalan Enterprises, Richmond circle, Bangalore and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/-
p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
As per the medical records i.e., Ex-P11-wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e.,bimalleolar fracture left knee.
The doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Further petitioner has produced Ex-P12 discharge summary of M.S.Ramaiah memorial hospital which reveals petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 23-2-2021 to 23-2- 2021 i.e., for 1 day.
Further petitioner has produced Ex-P76 discharge summary of Prolife Multispeciality hospital which reveals that petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 23-2- 2021 to 27-2-2021.

Further petitioner has produced Ex-P91 discharge summary of Prolife Multispeciality hospital which reveals that petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 23-2- 2021 to 25-2-2021 i.e., total for 5 days.
19. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Shankara K.C.- Medical record Technician at M.S.Ramaiah memorial hospital, Bangalore as PW.2 who has produced Ex-P81-auhorisation letter, Ex-P82-police intimation, Ex-P83-inpatient record and Ex-P84-3 x-rays.

Further petitioner got examined one Ragavendra T.G.-Medical record officer at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital, Bangalore as PW-3 who has produced Ex- P85-authorisation letter Ex-P86-MLC Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
5 intimation, Ex-P87-MLC note copy, Ex-P88- patient information form, Ex-P89-consent for admission record, Ex-P90-consent for surgery, Ex-P91 and 92-discharge summaries and Ex-P93-case sheet.

Further petitioner got examined Dr.B.Ramesh-orthopaedic surgeon at Victoria hospital, Bangalore as PW-4 who has stated that, petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., bimalleolar fracture of left ankle and underwent internal fixation of both malleolai.

PW-4 further stated that he examined the petitioner on 6-12-2022 for assessment of disability and complained of pain in left ankle, difficulty to squat on floor, difficulty to climb upstairs, difficulty to walk on slope, difficulty to stand on affected limb and difficulty to do the routine activities.
PW-4 further stated that radiological examination shows fracture united with implants n situ.
PW-4 assessed the permanent physical disability of 28% of left lower limb which is 14% to the wholebody.
20. During cross examination of PW-4 admitted that fractured bones are united.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.4 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.
21.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner was working as interior wood work supervisor, can do work with some disability.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 9%.

As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 36 to 40 is '15'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,43,000/- (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 15 X 9/100) is awarded under this head.

22. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e.,
bimalleolar fracture of left ankle and the doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
The petitioner took treatment as inpatient at M.S.Ramaiah hospital as inpatient on 23-2-2021 for one day.

Further as per discharge summary Ex-P76,
petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Prolife multi speciality hospital as inpatient from 23-2-2021 to 27-2-2021 for 5 days.
From Ex-P91 discharge summary reveals that petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 23-2-2021 to 25-2-2021.
From Ex-P93 it reveals that petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Prolife multi speciality hospital from 23-2-2021 to 23-2-202.
The petitioner has stated that he is suffering with permanent disablement and deformity to attend his work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.

On account of the accidental injuries the Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
6 petitioner being 38 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.

sentences.text: Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

23. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and operation undergone by him and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 5 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.75,000/- (15,000 X 5)
under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
24. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru and has taken treatment at M.S.Ramaiah hospital,
Bangalore, Prolife multi speciality hospital, Bangalore as inpatient and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 5 days and sustained injuries i.e., bimalleolar fracture of left ankle and underwent internal fixation of both malleolai and certainly,
it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.

Hence a sum of Rs.15,000/-
under this head.

25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
26. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked Ex-P14 to 30 medical prescriptions, Ex-P31 to 67 medical bills for Rs.91,075/-.
Further petitioner has produced Ex-P77 to 80 advance bills for Rs.55,600/-.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.1,46,675/-
under the head of medical expenses.

27. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

29. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

30. The respondent No.1 insurance company has taken the defence that the alleged policy particulars mentioned in petition i.e., policy No.0G18-170-00000153 is issued to the vehicle No.DL-1-RY-4747 from 8-5-2017 to 7-5-2018 and the said policy has not been issued in respect of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371 and moreover the said policy does not cover the date of accident i.e., on 23-2-2021.

No policy has been issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of the offending vehicle at the time of the accident and hence the policy details mentioned in the petition are false, fabricated and not issued by this respondent and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
As such there is no prima-facie contract between the owner of the offending vehicle and this respondent as on the date of accident to indemnify under the terms of the insurance contract.

In support of their contention, respondent No.2 got examined Jayanth Inamdar- Legal Manager as RW-1 who in his deposition has testified that the insurance policy Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
8 No.OG-18-1701-1831-00000153 as stated in the claim petition is not at all issued to the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371 and the insurance policy details mentioned in the claim petition are disclosing that it is a fake, fabricated one and there was no contract of insurance between 1st respondent and 2nd respondent as on the date of alleged accident.

sentences.text: The insurance policy No.0G-18-1701-1831-00000153 as stated in the claim petition is issued to the Toyota Etio cab bearing No.DL-1-RY-4747 and same is valid from 8-5-2017 to 7- 5-2018 and said insurance policy is issued in favour of Meru cab company Pvt., Ltd.,
It is further stated that the vehicle bearing No.DL-1-RY-4747 is not at all involved int he said alleged accident.

Hence it is clear that they have not at all issued any policy to auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371.
31.

Hence the insurance policy produced by the petitioner is fake insurance policy and no liability could be saddled or fixed upon their insurance company to indemnify the owner of the offending autorickshaw to pay any compensation to the petitioner arising out of the alleged accident.

Further argued that even respondent No.2 had given the complaint to the concerned jurisdictional police station and requested to take legal action against the culprit in respect of the forged and fabricated document.
Hence, petitioners case is based on the fake and fabricated documents which is illegal and not valid in the eyes of law.
32. In support of their contention got marked Ex-R1 to Ex-R3 documents.

On perusal of the documents produced by the respondent No.2, Ex-R1 is the insurance policy No.OG-18- 1701-1831-00000153 issued in respect of Meru cab company Toyota Etios company and respondent No.2 has filed the complaint to the police station to the conduct enquiry and investigation with regard to issuance of the fake policy bearing No.OG-18-1701-1831-00000153 in respect of the vehicle bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371.

sentences.text: On the other hand, respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle has not appeared before the court and contested the case.
Even though summons has been issued to the respondent No.1 several times, respondent No.1 did not appeared before the court and adduced any evidence.
Even petitioner has not produced any copy of the policy.
Even though counsel for the petitioner cross examined RW-1 at length, but nothing worth was elicited from his mouth.

Though petitioner counsel contended that Ex-R1 policy is created by the respondent, but petitioner has not disproved the Ex-R1 by producing the policy copy in respect of the offending vehicle alleged by them.
thus it clearly shows that the petitioner has given the policy Number which does not belongs to the offending vehicle.

even petitioner has not made any attempt to summon the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.1 and to call for the real policy details in respect of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
all these facts establishes that the policy No.OG-18-1701-1831-00000153 does not belongs to the offending vehicle.

33. Petitioner except stating number of the insurance policy which does not belongs to the offending vehicle has not made any attempt to secure the policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident from owner and also adduced evidence of respondent No.2.
34.

Having considered the evidence and examining the submissions made at bar, first of all it be noted that evidence of RW-1 was essentially regarding fake policy of offending vehicle autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371 as such evidence was against respondent No.1 owner of said vehicle,
however said respondent No.1 did not cross examine that witness at all.

Even in the Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/
9

sentences.text: cross-examination of RW-1 by counsel for the petitioner nothing substantive has come on the record.
No suggestion has been given to the witness that the grounds on the basis of which witness RW-1 tried to prove the policy being fake are incorrect.

In the absence of any such suggestion and nothing substantive come in the cross examination, this Tribunal finds that witness has clearly given specific and cogent reasons duly supported with the insurance policy Ex-R1 which belongs to the different vehicle in respect of the 2017-2018 generally issued by respondent No.2 company.

In such circumstance this tribunal finds that insurance company has proved by preponderance of probability that insurance policy of offending vehicle as relied upon being fake and does not belongs to the offending vehicle and it was issued in respect of another vehicle in the year 2017-2018.

It is pertinent to note here that even inspite of the contention and the defence raised by the respondent No.2 petitioner has not made any attempt to produce any insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident there was no insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
35. No doubt regarding the claim of insurance company policy being fake, separate complaint has been filed by respondent No.2 company.
However filing of complaint to policy authority is just a ritual, when otherwise the fact of insurance policy being fake is proved by other evidence which remained uncontroverted.

It is settled law that when insurance company has prima-facie shown that serial number of the policy being issued in respect of the different vehicle Toyoto Etios of Meru cab company private limited during the year 2017-2018 ,that fact stand proved by preponderance of probability.
Thus this Tribunal finds that respondent No.2 has proved the insurance policy relied upon is fake.

In this case no directions can be given to the insurance company for making the payment of compensation amount and then to recover from respondent No.1 because there was no contractual liability of respondent No.2/insurance company at all to pay the compensation when the insurance policy in itself is a fake and does not impose any binding duty to reimburse the amount of compensation by respondent No.2.
As such the liability to pay compensation is upon respondent No.1 only.

36. Therefore the respondent No.1 being the RC owner is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 answered as Partly in the Affirmative'.
37. ISSUE NO.3: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,94,700/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The petition against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.

Respondents  JUDGMENT This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

opennyai_summary.facts:
On the date of accident, offending vehicle was not holding effective DL which is in contravention of the conditions and MV Act.
The offending vehicle was having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply in the public place, in this regard jurisdictional police have fled charge sheet u/s 66 and 192 of MV Act and there is a violation of provisions of MV Act.
The petitioner has suppressed the true fact and colluded with the first respondent and jurisdictional police and filed false case against the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the autrickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371 on 23-2-2021 at about 8.30 a.m. at New BEL road, near HP, petrol bunk, Bengaluru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate? from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though respondent No.2 has examined the Legal Manager of the insurance company as RW-1, but RW-1 is not an eye witness.
Apart from this, there is no material to prove that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his avocation and income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/-
p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.4 has assessed the disability on the higher side.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner was working as interior wood work supervisor, can do work with some disability.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
Hence the insurance policy produced by the petitioner is fake insurance policy and no liability could be saddled or fixed upon their insurance company to indemnify the owner of the offending autorickshaw to pay any compensation to the petitioner arising out of the alleged accident.
In such circumstance this tribunal finds that insurance company has proved by preponderance of probability that insurance policy of offending vehicle as relied upon being fake and does not belongs to the offending vehicle and it was issued in respect of another vehicle in the year 2017-2018.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident there was no insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
However filing of complaint to policy authority is just a ritual, when otherwise the fact of insurance policy being fake is proved by other evidence which remained uncontroverted.
It is settled law that when insurance company has prima-facie shown that serial number of the policy being issued in respect of the different vehicle Toyoto Etios of Meru cab company private limited during the year 2017-2018 ,that fact stand proved by preponderance of probability.
Thus this Tribunal finds that respondent No.2 has proved the insurance policy relied upon is fake.
In this case no directions can be given to the insurance company for making the payment of compensation amount and then to recover from respondent No.1 because there was no contractual liability of respondent No.2/insurance company at all to pay the compensation when the insurance policy in itself is a fake and does not impose any binding duty to reimburse the amount of compensation by respondent No.2.
As such the liability to pay compensation is upon respondent No.1 only.

37. ISSUE NO.3: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,94,700/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The petition against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
The respondent No.1 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
